en: awful noises at night.
Last night it scared me clean out of bed!
Say, have you heard?
The guest staying at this inn,
word is she's an opera singer
Seems she's on her way to the big city.
All sorts of travelers stop by and move on.
That's the kind of town Calstatt is
Just about the time Calstatt began to prosper,
note: Same as #6717 (slice 083); followed by shared #6718 'if I remember right.'

en: So she's the innkeeper
She looks as though she's stronger than
most of the men around here.
What's this, a customer at this hour?
Oh, it's you. You needn't come this late,
you're welcome to drop by in the daytime.
There's a free room, so I'll show you up.
In that case, yes, please.
Right, this way.
Aaaaaaaagh
note: Scream carries the length itself: shared #4580 (～) is '' and #414 adds '!'.

en: I'm sorry. You'll be able to go back once the war is over.
If it has come to this, it can't be helped.
To make Luisa a woman worthy of
the Stanberg family,
I shall train her most thoroughly myself!
Having heard my husband out,
I did once give my blessing to their marriage,
but I simply cannot accept it.
Of all people, the bride is to be Luisa!
When there are any number of
fine young ladies out there...
I just cannot accept it!
I always hoped Stuart would find someone
suitable, but...
It can't be helped, I suppose.
I never imagined my husband
would give his permission.
My husband's persuasion and Stuart's resolve
won me over, let us say.
If you had a younger sister,
this marriage might never have happened.
My husband would never allow such a match.
I will find a noble young lady worthy of
the Stanberg family, mark my words.
So it was true after all!
Honestly, that Luisa.
Wanting a suitable woman for Stuart,
I've long searched for marriage prospects,
yet he never says a word about it.
I should have thrown Luisa out
far sooner.
Before it ever came to this!
I've told my husband about Luisa,
but he won't take me seriously.
A maid like Luisa simply
must not be kept on!
Really, that Luisa! Why must she keep
making one blunder after another?
Oh, I'm afraid you've overheard
something unseemly again.
That girl is always like this...
Perhaps I ought to dismiss her?
Keeping a maid like Luisa around
is utterly unnecessary!
She's a maid, yet she can't even do
something this simple? Honestly...
I'm afraid you've overheard something unseemly.
We have several maids in our household,
and one of them, a girl called "Luisa,"
is forever blundering. She's hopeless.
Why must we keep a maid who can't even
make a bed in this house, I wonder?
Stuart's bride, too,
must be a lady of high standing.
I must find someone suitable for him.
You are a guest with the standing
worthy of this house.
Why, your manners have such refinement.
The Stanbergs are a house of high standing,
so our guests, and I myself, must be noble,
My own family is kin to Prussian royalty.
